extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of poetics/dramatic theory (playwrights, literary critics)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria drawn from Aristotle's Poetics (with commentary) for composing and judging tragedy and epic: what to imitate, the parts of tragedy, unity and probability, diction and style, and practical stage considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation: one thing to imitate (threefold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoniam enim Poeta est Imitator ... cum tria sint, unum quid semper imitetur: aut sane — qualia fuerunt aut sunt, — aut quaferuntur & videntur, — aut qualia esse oportet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poet imitates either (a) what was, (b) what is, or (c) what ought to be; these are rendered by diction, voices, and metaphors. Choose a coherent object of imitation and express it through appropriate linguistic and figurative means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid imitating the impossible (vitium per se)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per se quidem Vitium est cum aggrediatur imitari id quod fit extra facultatem suam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is a fundamental fault to depict events or states that are absolutely impossible for the art to produce, unless such depiction serves a legitimate artistic end (e.g., to excite wonder). If the impossibility could have been, the error is mitigated; examples and exceptions (e.g., Hector's pursuit) must be judged by whether the end is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid incorrect imitation (vitium per accidens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per accidens vero, cum haud recte imitatur; sed Equum fingit ambo dextra crura promoventem. aut contra singulas artes peccat ... si ea, quae effici non possunt, finxit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fault occurs when imitation is done wrongly (badly executed) or when the poet contravenes the norms of a separate art (e.g., medicine). Distinguish mistakes of ignorance from deliberate departures; weigh severity (e.g., factual ignorance about natural details is less blameworthy than poor craftsmanship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction and linguistic appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Hæc autem exponuntur Dictione, aut Linguis & Metaphoris. multæ etiam affectiones sunt Dictionis. has enim concedimus Poetis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose diction, voice, and metaphors suited to the material. Consider accent, voice, customary usages, ambiguity, and metaphorical extension. Solve problems of diction by examining how words signify and by preferring usages that fit speaker, context, and probable meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum of speech and action (decorum/indecorum)
rubrics_metrics.description: De decoro aut indecoro dicto aut facto alicujus non solum animadverten dum est ratione habita ipfius facti aut dicti, utrum honestum an turpe sit, sed facientis etiam & dicentis, — cui sane, aut quando, aut quo, aut propter quod; scilicet, aut propter majus Bonum, ut fiat; aut majus Malum, ut non fiat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether language or deed is fitting not only by the deed itself but by who speaks/acts, when, why, and to what end. An action or speech may be decorous in one context and indecorous in another depending on purpose and agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle words that seem to mean the contrary (subcontrary meanings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oportet vero quando vox aliqua videtur significare quid Subcontrarium, considerare quot modis significet eo quod dictum fit ... quot autem modis significet fic apparebit, si quis praecipue interpretetur vocem sensu maxime contrario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a word appears to signify the opposite, analyze the modes of signification and interpret according to the most plausible sense; beware of absurd or prejudiced readings that render lines vitious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to reproaches (five species of objection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has igitur Reprehensiones ex quinque speciebus ducunt: aut sane ut impossibilia, aut absurda, aut noxia, aut subcontraria, aut praeter ipsius artis normam. Solutiones ex his numeris ducendae: sunt autem duodecim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticisms of a poet’s work fall into five kinds (impossible, absurd, harmful, subcontrary, beyond the art's norm); practical responses and solutions can be drawn (the text enumerates twelve methods to resolve them). Use these categories to test and defend choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot (Fabula) as the first and soul of tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Principium ergo & quasi Anima Tragediae est Fabula. estque ea Actionis, & eorum, qui per hanc maxime agunt imitatio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plot (action) is the central element of tragedy; composition should prioritize a well-constructed, complete action carried by the agents. Ensure the plot shows a coherent sequence of cause-and-effect events forming a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of action: one whole, single action
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabulam vero rages unam esse & a Actione una integra. ... Si enim quis pulcherrimos confundat colores, non ita delectabit, ac si creta certam delineet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tragedy should represent a single, unified action rather than a patchwork of unrelated episodes. Multiple distinct actions make the whole incoherent; if several separate events are imitated, the work becomes episodic rather than a single tragedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and economy of imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Porro, eo melior est quod imitatio breviore termino includatur. id enim, quod confertius, jucundius est quam id, quod longo tempore distrahitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shorter, more concentrated imitation is preferable: compression enhances pleasure. Prefer concise realization of the action over drawn-out, diffuse narration (example: Oedipus compressed rather than stretched to epic length).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragedy vs Epic: which attains its end better
rubrics_metrics.description: Si igitur Tragœdia his omnibus excellat, & Artis etiam munere ... manifestum est ut melior fit quam Epopœia, quoniam finem suum magis assequatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate genres by how well they achieve their ends: tragedy may be superior to epic if it more effectively attains its artistic purpose, even if epic has length and multiplicity of incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character (Mores) as second part of tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Secundum, Mores. — Tertium, Sententia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters (their dispositions and behavior) are essential — they must be appropriate, consistent, and such that their actions arise naturally from character. Moral example and the effect on the audience (imitation of morals) are important to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought / Sententia (ideas and reasoning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tertium, Sententia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expressed thoughts and arguments (sententiae) should be appropriate to characters and situation, exhibiting coherent reasoning and serving the plot’s development and thematic ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus (spectacle, scenery, costume) as auxiliary
rubrics_metrics.description: Hæc est Sexta Tragediae pars, quam ... Apparatum. ... illa continentur omnia, quae oculis Spectatorum subjiciuntur; ut Ornatus Scenae, vestimenta Histrionum, Personae, cum Fabula aliqua recitatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage apparatus (scenery, costumes, spectacle) contributes to effect but is not the essence of tragedy; it should support the plot and recognition without substituting for good plot or character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chorus and its proper function
rubrics_metrics.description: Achoris partes Chorus officiumque: Defendat: neu quid medios intercinat actus, non ein conducat & haerent apt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chorus has particular duties and should not interrupt the action improperly; it must fit the structure of acts and support, rather than fragment, the dramatic flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of gesture and physical action
rubrics_metrics.description: Omnis tamen Gesticulatio non repudianda est, siquidem neque omnis Saltatio, sed impudicorum tantum, — vitio enim dabatur Callippidi ... Porro, Tragoedia etiam tam munere suo fungitur sine Gesticulazione, quam Epopoeia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some gesture and movement are permissible and useful; avoid excessive or indecent gesticulation. A tragedy can function without extravagant physical display; gestures should be measured and suited to the audience and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of music and metre where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Etenim licet ei Metro uti, & (quod excellentissimum est) Musicam habet & Apparatum, per quem voluptates perquam evidenter percipiunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meter and musical elements enhance pleasure when aligned with the work’s nature. Use rhythm, verse, and music to increase clarity and emotional effect, but ensure they serve the imitation and are not gratuitous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition (Agnitio) must be plausible and integral
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliquando autem ambos oportet agnoscere. ... sumitque illud ex Euripidis Fabula ... Ceu phigenia Orefti cognita est missione Epistolae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognitions should arise naturally from tokens, signs, or credible events (not from contrived means). They must fit the plot’s logic and be intelligible to the audience; false reasoning-based recognitions are an identified subtype (agnitio ex falsa ratiocinatione).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability and plausibility (verisimilitude)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primum enim, fi ea, quae extra facultatem sint artis suae, finxit, peccatum fuit: recte tamen se habeat, si Finem suum consequatur. ... id, quod impossibile est & probabile tamen videtur, optabilius est, quam quod non probabile sit n(possibile).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor what is probable and exhibits verisimilitude. The poet may sometimes employ the improbable if it produces a preferable effect, but maintain audience belief by ensuring events feel plausible within the work's internal logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid gratuitous absurdity or vacuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Aqua vero tum Objectio est, & vacuitas Rationis, & Pravitas, cum, nulla urgente necessitate, nihilominus adhibeatur Absur-dum, sicut Euripides adhibuit improbitatem geeti, & in Oreste Menelai.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not introduce absurdities or empty reasoning without necessity; such inclusions are faults. Use extraordinary devices only when they are required to achieve the work's end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral/imitative example: consider effects on audience conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Cauſe ex Re oritur Poetica scil. — Studium Imitationis nobis a natura infitum — & Oblectatio e in cernendis Imitamentis (ii, percipimus). ... qui inducuntur in Fabulam, quique artificio Poetae exprimuntur: hore nim vitz prodest, nam qui spectant, cum her in Fabulis laudari plau-suque excipi vident, ad ea facta imitanda excitantur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that representations of actions may serve as examples that the audience imitates. Poets should consider whether praise or applause for certain acts might encourage immoral imitation and weigh social effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in representing known facts (avoid implausible ignorance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non est autem verisimile, cum ipse ei in regno successerit, non statim ipsum Auctores illius necis investigatum fuisset. Hoc tamen ideo finxit Poeta, quia si, recenti adhuc re, studii aliquid in hoc facto indagando posuisset Oedipus, subito auctorem illius necis extitisse cognovisset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making characters inexplicably ignorant of things the audience knows would be investigated; such lapses harm plausibility. If a poet departs from expected inquiry, it must be justified to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate personae selection and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Inimicosque sibi homines, aut turpes viros omnibus contumeliis vexant, quz definitae personae nomina quibus une habent. ... Poetis solvere fabulas acceptas a veteribus non licere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose characters (and their names) so they coherently represent roles and social types. Be cautious when altering well-known traditional plots or characters; deviations should be defensible within the work's logic and aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal constraints and economy of the action (time management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectandum Aristoteles tradit tempus, quod consumunt Tragoediae quas moris fit (apud Athenienses). ... Si sane quam plurime Tragoediae agende sint, harum unagæque ad Clepsydram (ut Rhetorum mos est) agenda est, sive certo tempore ad finem perducenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect practical temporal limits of performance: structure acts so that required scenes fit customary performance time (e.g., Clepsydra timing). Ensure the sequence and duration of actions are manageable and contribute to unity.
